author: @offthepressnews
title_or_hook: JPMorgan Chase vendor cyberattack, Visa and Mastercard too
summary: JPMorgan Chase said third-party service providers were hit by a cyberattack and attackers accessed vendor-held marketing data that may include some customer names and email addresses, with no disruption to its services. Independent coverage the same day widens the event: Visa and Mastercard confirmed vendor incidents of their own, a group calling itself n0n claimed the leaks, and the bank said it will contact affected customers directly and offer complimentary credit monitoring where appropriate. Corroborated this run by five independent reports tracing to the bank's Nov 19 statement. The leaked-file contents reported by Cybernews (about 16,000 customer emails, some phone numbers/account IDs, tied to the invitation-only Reserve program, plus 100+ employee emails) are UNCONFIRMED - the bank has not confirmed counts, named the vendors, or confirmed the group's responsibility, and Reuters could not independently verify the leaked data's authenticity. The bank states no connection to its earlier-week outage. Filed as the Family Shield exposure-audit lane's current vendor-breach case study: the exposure vector was the vendors' marketing data, not the banks' own systems. No test; the only follow-up is passive, if a Chase/Visa/Mastercard notice arrives.
metrics_or_datasets: about 16,000 customer emails in reported leaked files (UNCONFIRMED)
100+ employee emails (UNCONFIRMED)

author: @drivelinebaseball
title_or_hook: Maikel Garcia: same swing, different approach
summary: Driveline swing-decision breakdown of Maikel Garcia (figures as posted): his bat speed and swing length were essentially flat year over year, while his heart-zone swing rate fell sharply, his barrel rate and expected production on those pitches fell with it, his full-count chase rate rose and his walk rate fell - the post's thesis is that indecision, not mechanics, cost the power. The caption closes with his track record (2025 All-Star/Gold Glove; 2026 WBC MVP line as posted) and is truncated at the tail in the post view. Method template: hold the mechanics constant, then read the decision layer (what he swung at, in which counts). Cross-sport pattern for the GSE reasoning layer - 'same tools, worse decisions' is exactly the QB read Garrett's engine is built to make - and a clean explainer format for the Content OS: one thesis, one held-constant, one moving layer. All figures single-source as posted; the four slides are muted video clips, so any spoken layer is lost.
